findings.issue_text: [BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, which PRCommentWorkflow does not inherit from, so the call raises AttributeError. Every GitHub and GitLab merged-PR comment built via get_comment_body in src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:406 and gitlab/integration.py:254 crashes with AttributeError ('PRCommentWorkflow' has no attribute '_truncate_title') instead of rendering the comment body.

[BUG] fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with events.values() via zip, but nodestore.backend.get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id that omits missing nodes, so any missing event shifts the values and mislabels error events with the wrong title/message/timestamp. When one or more error events are absent from nodestore (expired/retention), every subsequent error is paired with another event's data, and the chronological merge in gen_request_data emits wrong error messages to the Seer summarization request; users get a breadcrumb summary referencing errors that never occurred.

[BUG] fetch_error_details zips error_ids with the values of the nodestore.get_multi result dict, misaligning event IDs with event data whenever any node is missing or the dict order differs from input order. nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids) returns a dict keyed by node_id containing only the nodes it found (and in its own iteration order); when a node is missing or reordered, zip(error_ids, events.values()) pairs the wrong event_id with the wrong payload, so the summary sent to Seer attributes error titles/messages to the wrong error IDs — silently corrupted LLM input with no error raised.

[BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template is a @staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration but calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, while _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, not PRCommentWorkflow. Unless PRCommentWorkflow happens to inherit CommitContextIntegration, the merged-PR comment path for GitHub and GitLab raises AttributeError ('PRCommentWorkflow' has no attribute '_truncate_title') the first time a merged PR comment is rendered, breaking PR bot commenting entirely; the new truncation/environment behavior also has no test in the diff covering the template path.

[BUG] The mutual-exclusion cross-field validation uses truthiness on initial_data (if self.initial_data.get("age")/get("timestamp")), so age=0 or timestamp=0 bypasses the exclusion and a report containing both fields validates successfully. Per the Reporting API working draft, a report carries exactly one of age/timestamp; a browser (or crafted client) sending age=0 alongside a timestamp passes validation, and the downstream consumer that assumes one-of semantics processes ambiguous data — the acceptance criterion the serializer was added to enforce is silently violated for zero-valued fields.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten serializer accepts a report with neither age nor timestamp (both required=False with no one-of check), and there are no tests in this diff for the new BrowserReportSerializer at all. The Reporting API spec requires exactly one of age or timestamp per report; the new validation layer (the diff's stated purpose) has no spec coverage, so regressions in the cross-field rules — including the currently missing one-of requirement — ship undetected.

[ADVISORY] The new error-context path (query_replay_instance, process_raw_response, fetch_error_details, enable_error_context gating) is non-trivial new behavior with no tests in this diff. A regression in the new chronological merge logic in gen_request_data (e.g. event.get("timestamp", 0) defaulting to 0 forcing all errors to the front, or error_events sorted inside get_request_data mutating shared state per pagination page) breaks breadcrumb summaries with no test to catch it; the enable_error_context=false escape hatch is also unverified.

[ADVISORY] get_request_data sorts the error_events list in place, and error_events is the same list captured by the functools.partial across every paginate() page invocation. The mutation is currently idempotent (sorting an already-sorted list), but the shared mutable state threaded through partial means any future change to per-page filtering or filtering by timestamp window inside get_request_data will silently alter later pages' error output; the sort should happen once at construction.

[ADVISORY] The new enable_error_context=false gating uses default-true truthy string comparison, but the diff does not document or test the sibling behavior that error context fetch runs an unconditional nodestore.get_multi plus a Snuba query_replay_instance call on every request even when no errors exist. Every summarize request now pays a full replay-instance Snuba query plus a nodestore multi-get regardless of whether any error IDs exist; clients on the old path (no error context support) get a hot-path latency regression with no way to disable the Snuba query itself — only the nodestore fetch is gated by the query param.

[ADVISORY] This PR, titled 'Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System', flips the global default of DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT from "low" to "off" (and the corresponding projectoption in src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py line 205), which is unrelated to replay deletion and is a user-visible behavior change for every org not pinning the option. Orgs relying on the default get autofix silently disabled after this deploy; whoever merges this for the replay-delete feature ships an unrequested behavioral change to all customers and cannot trace it to any stated requirement.

[ADVISORY] Two shipped data migrations (0917 and 0920 converting org saved searches to views) are gutted to `return`, dead-code removal that has nothing to do with the stated replay bulk-delete intent. Ops engineers reviewing this PR for replay deletion will miss that a data migration was retroactively disabled; the change belongs in its own PR with its own justification, and bundling it hides a data-integrity decision from reviewers of the replay feature.

[ADVISORY] The removal of ParameterizationRegexExperiment, the corresponding option registration in src/sentry/options/defaults.py (lines 2627-2632), and the isinstance dispatch simplification is a grouping-engine refactor unrelated to the replay bulk-delete intent of this PR. Anyone bisecting a grouping regression or auditing feature-flag cleanup now lands on a 'replays bulk delete' commit; the coupling also means reverting the replay feature reverts the grouping experiment teardown.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint is rewritten from a dataclass to a DRF serializer with new validation semantics (age/timestamp mutual exclusion, per-report 422 responses), which is unrelated to replay bulk delete. The PR's stated scope gives reviewers of browser reporting no context — the new mutual-exclusion validation rejects reports browsers legitimately send (e.g., an Editor's Draft report carrying both fields is silently dropped as 422), a contract change smuggled in under an unrelated title.

[ADVISORY] This diff substantially extends the breadcrumb summarization endpoint with error-event fetching, chronological merging, and a new `enable_error_context` query param — feature work adjacent to but distinct from the stated bulk-delete system. The new undocumented raw query param `enable_error_context` (line ~83) is behavior with no requirement traceability and no feature flag; it rides along in a PR whose title promises only deletion, so its Snuba/nodestore call additions on every GET are unreviewed as a scope item.

[ADVISORY] Adding processing_deadline_duration (30/300/120) to webhook delivery taskworker configs, plus the similar deadline added in src/sentry/tasks/auth/check_auth.py, is infrastructure tuning unrelated to the replay bulk-delete system. These deadline changes alter task retry/redelivery semantics for webhooks and auth checks; bundled into a replay PR they bypass the scrutiny of the owners of those subsystems, and a revert of the replay feature silently reverts them.

[ADVISORY] The GitHub/GitLab merged-PR comment template is redesigned (new template constant, title truncation, environment suffix) — user-facing integration output changes with no traceability to the replay bulk-delete requirement. Every customer with the GitHub/GitLab PR bot gets differently formatted PR comments after this deploy; the change also adds a per-issue `get_recommended_event()` call on the comment path (line 585), a new DB/nodestore cost on a hot integration path hidden inside an unrelated PR.

[ADVISORY] The workflow-engine refactor (hoisting get_slow_conditions_for_groups, threading dcg_to_slow_conditions through two functions, swapping logger to log_context in processors/workflow.py) is untraceable to any replay bulk-delete requirement. Workflow engine owners get semantics changes (including a new info-level log on no-slow-condition DCGs) shipped under a replay PR title; this makes blame/bisect and selective revert of the actual feature impossible.

[ADVISORY] New analytics event registration and instrumentation of the preprod artifact assemble endpoint is unrelated scope riding in this PR. Analytics event schema decisions land unreviewed by the preprod/telemetry owners; a revert of the replay feature would silently remove the event, breaking dashboards built on it.

[ADVISORY] Rewriting the feedback-summary LLM prompt (separator change, 55-word hard cap) is unrelated to the stated replay bulk-delete intent. Prompt engineering changes materially alter AI output for all feedback-summary users and cannot be tested by this PR's replay-delete review; bundling them makes the change effectively unreviewed.

[ADVISORY] Adding an `equations` passthrough parameter to run_top_events_timeseries_query is API-surface work for the logs dataset with no requirement traceability in a replay bulk-delete PR. The new parameter is accepted but no call site in this diff passes it — a ships-inert signature change that logs-dataset owners never reviewed under this PR's scope.

[BUG] fetch_error_details zips error_ids against events.values() of the nodestore.get_multi result, so when any node_id is missing from the returned dict, the remaining ids get paired with the wrong events' data. For a replay with one or more error events purged from nodestore, every subsequent id/data pair is shifted by one, so the LLM breadcrumb summary attributes the wrong title/message to the wrong error and can misorder errors entirely; a simple `[(id, events.get(node_id)) for id in error_ids]` lookup keyed by node_id would be correct.

[BUG] gen_request_data interleaves error timestamps against rrweb segment event timestamps that are on different scales/types: nodestore event `timestamp` is a second-scale value (often an ISO string, per data.get('timestamp')), while segment events carry millisecond-epoch numbers, so the comparison `error_events[error_idx]['timestamp'] < event.get('timestamp', 0)` compares incomparable units (and can raise TypeError comparing str to int). Error log messages are emitted at the wrong positions in the interleaved chronology (or the endpoint 500s when a string timestamp is compared against an int), so the breadcrumb summary sent to Seer reports errors out of order relative to user actions; the fetch must normalize both to one unit before sorting/interleaving.

[BUG] The new DRF serializer makes `body` a required DictField and `url` a required URLField, which is a narrowing of the previously-accepted report shape: the Reporting API spec permits reports whose `body` is absent (e.g. crash and some policy reports) and an empty `url`, all of which the old dataclass constructor accepted. Browsers sending spec-legal reports with no body or empty url now receive HTTP 422 instead of 200, so those reports are silently dropped and the collector's metric undercounts real browser reports; body should be required=False/allow_null and url should tolerate empty string per the spec.

[ADVISORY] The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators use truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")`), so `age: 0` is treated as absent and a report carrying both `timestamp` and `age: 0` passes validation, and a report with neither field is also accepted even though the spec requires exactly one. Malformed reports that violate the Working-Draft/Editor's-Draft split leak into the metrics tag path and skew counts; the next editor debugging 'which spec sent this report' gets misleading data.

[ADVISORY] The preprod_artifact.api.assemble analytics event is recorded before the feature-gate check, so unauthorized and feature-disabled requests are counted identically to real assembles. Whoever consumes this analytics event to measure assemble adoption gets inflated counts including 403-gated requests; move the record() after the features.has check.

[ADVISORY] The `enable_error_context` flag is parsed as a raw query string compared with `.lower() == "false"` (default "true"), a stringly-typed boolean with no named constant and no shared client/server definition, so any other falsy value ("0", "False" handled, but "no", "off", empty string) silently means true. The next caller toggling the flag with a value other than the exact string 'false' gets error context silently included and has no compile-checked constant to discover the contract from.

[BUG] fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with nodestore results via zip(error_ids, events.values()), but get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id that drops missing nodes, so positional pairing misassigns titles/messages/timestamps to the wrong error_id. When any requested event is absent from nodestore, every subsequent error event in the list is labeled with the wrong event id and wrong title, so the LLM breadcrumb summary attributes one error's message to another error.

[BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, and PRCommentWorkflow is a separate ABC that does not inherit from it, so the call raises AttributeError. Every merged-PR comment containing at least one issue (GitHub and GitLab) crashes with AttributeError instead of rendering the comment body.

[ADVISORY] The default for sentry:autofix_automation_tuning is silently flipped from "low" to "off" (also in src/sentry/constants.py:724) inside a PR titled "Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System", with no feature flag or migration for projects that relied on the old default. All existing projects that never explicitly set the option stop getting autofix automation on new issues after deploy; this product-behavior change has no explicit acceptance trail in the PR's stated objective and cannot be rolled back without a code deploy.

[ADVISORY] The 0917 and 0920 data migrations' conversion logic is deleted and replaced with a no-op `return` while the migration numbers are retained, relying on a comment asserting they were never run; any environment that did execute the buggy version will have its partially-converted state silently frozen. Deployments where the original migration ran with data errors keep corrupted/partial GroupSearchView rows with no idempotent re-run, and org-level saved searches remain unconverted; the fix depends entirely on the unverifiable claim that 0921 covers every environment.

[ADVISORY] Neither age nor timestamp is required by the serializer, so a report containing neither field validates successfully, contradicting the Working-Draft-vs-Editor's-Draft mutual-exclusion intent the cross-validation was written to enforce. Malformed browser reports missing both fields are accepted with HTTP 200 and counted in metrics, so the collector's validation figures overstate real report volume and downstream consumers assuming a timestamp get None.

[ADVISORY] The merged-PR comment format silently changed from `- ‼️ **{title}** \`{subtitle}\` [View Issue]({url})` to `* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}`, dropping the culprit subtitle entirely, with no visible acceptance that removing culprit context from PR comments is intended. Users who relied on the culprit line in merged-PR comments lose that signal after deploy with no feature gate or release note in this PR's stated objective.

[ADVISORY] The new validation-failure path logs the entire raw attacker-supplied report body (`extra={..."raw_report": report}`) at warning level. Browser reports contain page URLs, user agents, and CSP violation details (which can include injected query-string values from end users); anyone on the internet can POST arbitrary payloads to this CSRF-exempt, unauthenticated endpoint, filling logs with attacker-chosen content and potential PII at unbounded volume — log injection/PII-leak vector introduced by this diff's logging call.

[ADVISORY] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template interpolates raw, unescaped issue titles and environment names into a Markdown template that is posted to GitHub/GitLab PR comments. Issue titles and environment names originate from ingested events (attacker-controllable by anyone who can send events to the project); a title containing Markdown/HTML link syntax (e.g. `[click](https://evil.example)` or an image tag) is rendered as-is in the bot's PR comment on the customer's repository, enabling content spoofing/link injection through a trusted Sentry bot account.

[BUG] fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with nodestore results by position instead of key: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` zips the request order against a dict's values, and nodestore.backend.get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id that omits (or None-fills) missing nodes, so once any node is missing or the dict ordering differs from error_ids, the wrong event's title/message is attached to the wrong error id. The `if data is not None` guard filters the shifted pairs, so the endpoint silently reports the wrong error title/message for a given error id (or drops valid errors) whenever one of the fetched nodes is missing — exactly the case the None guard exists for.

[ADVISORY] The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators use truthiness (`if self.initial_data.get("age")`) and neither field is required, so a report with age=0 and a timestamp, or a report with neither age nor timestamp, passes validation despite violating the 'exactly one of the two' spec semantics the comments claim to enforce. Clients sending age=0 alongside a timestamp (legitimate per the Working Draft) get an incorrect 422, and malformed reports with neither field are accepted with HTTP 200 and counted in metrics, skewing the browser_report_type adoption figures this endpoint was instrumented to gather.

[BUG] The new null check for max_segment_id returns an empty filename list, silently skipping deletion of recording segment files whenever the ClickHouse aggregate returns NULL, which conflates 'no segments tracked in the aggregate' with 'no segment files exist in blob storage'. Replays that have recording segment files in object storage but a NULL max_segment_id (due to delayed aggregate computation, backfill gaps, or replays whose rows pre-date segment tracking) will have their segment files permanently retained past the retention window or after a GDPR deletion request — silent data retention violation with no error surfaced.

[ADVISORY] Two shipped migration files (0917 and 0920) are gutted into no-ops and defer all conversion to 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py, which is not visible in the shown diff — if any self-hosted deployment already applied the original 0917 or 0920 migrations, the django_migrations table marks them as applied while the file content no longer performs the work, and correctness depends entirely on 0921 being present and idempotent. Self-hosted operators upgrading through this change must trust that 0921 exists, covers the same data set with the corrected filter, and uses an idempotent upsert; if 0921 is missing, mis-ordered in the migration graph, or has a narrower WHERE clause than the originals, org-level saved searches are silently lost during upgrade with no error and no rollback path.

[ADVISORY] Gutting 0920 (which added the owner_id__isnull=False filter over 0917) creates a migration-history hazard: any environment that partially applied 0917 before erroring will have some SavedSearch rows already converted to GroupSearchView, and the surviving update_or_create in 0921 must use the exact same natural-key lookup (organization, user_id, name) to avoid creating duplicate GroupSearchView rows for the same SavedSearch. If 0921's lookup key or filter differs from the originals, partial converts from a failed 0917 run produce duplicate or orphaned GroupSearchView entries that surface to end users as duplicated saved searches in the Issues UI after upgrade.

[BUG] validate_timestamp/validate_age use truthiness checks on `self.initial_data.get("age")` / `.get("timestamp")` so a legitimate value of 0 is treated as absent, defeating the mutual-exclusion validation entirely. A report sending `age: 0` alongside `timestamp` passes validate_timestamp's guard (0 is falsy) and is accepted with both fields present, so the spec-invariant the code claims to enforce is silently violated; symmetrically `timestamp: 0` is treated as absent and a report carrying both age and timestamp=0 is accepted instead of 422.

[BUG] The validation error message in validate_timestamp is inverted relative to the check: it raises when a timestamp is present and age is ALSO present, but the text says "If timestamp is present, age must be absent" — and validate_age's message describes the opposite field pair, so the 422 body misdescribes which field is at fault. A client sending both fields gets a message blaming timestamp validation when the conflicting field is age (and vice versa from validate_age), misdirecting integrators debugging rejected reports; the error shape is right but the content names the wrong field.

[BUG] fetch_error_details zips `error_ids` against `events.values()` from nodestore.get_multi, but get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id containing only the found nodes, so when any node is missing the remaining values shift position and are paired with the wrong error IDs. When one or more error events are missing/evicted from nodestore, every subsequent error ID in the list is paired with a different event's data (wrong title, message, timestamp), and the resulting summary request silently mixes up which errors occurred — corrupt AI-generated context with no error surfaced.

[ADVISORY] fetch_error_details catches Exception broadly, reports via sentry_sdk.capture_exception, and returns [] so the summarize endpoint proceeds with breadcrumbs only, silently dropping all error context. Users of the replay summarization feature get a breadcrumb-only summary with no indication that error context was requested and failed, and operators only see it if they sample the capture_exception; a persistent nodestore outage degrades every summary silently.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer`, both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False`, and the only cross-field checks are `validate_timestamp` (errors if `age` is present) and `validate_age` (errors if `timestamp` is present). The finding’s claim that there are no tests is incorrect (the diff adds many tests in `test_browser_reporting_collector.py`), but there is indeed no test covering the “missing both age and timestamp” case, so this bug would go undetected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new error-context path (query_replay_instance, process_raw_response, fetch_error_details, enable_error_context gating) is non-trivial new behavior with no tests in this diff. A regression in the new chronological merge logic in gen_request_data (e.g. event.get("timestamp", 0) defaulting to 0 forcing all errors to the front, or error_events sorted inside get_request_data mutating shared state per pagination page) breaks breadcrumb summaries with no test to catch it; the enable_error_context=false escape hatch is also unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* add tests covering the new error-context behavior in `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint`: `test_get_with_error` and `test_get_with_error_context_disabled` exercise `query_replay_instance`/`process_raw_response` and the `enable_error_context=false` gating, and `test_get_request_data` now verifies chronological merging of `error_events` with breadcrumb events (including differing timestamps). Therefore the claim that this new behavior has “no tests in this diff” and that the escape hatch is “unverified” is contradicted by the added test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] get_request_data sorts the error_events list in place, and error_events is the same list captured by the functools.partial across every paginate() page invocation. The mutation is currently idempotent (sorting an already-sorted list), but the shared mutable state threaded through partial means any future change to per-page filtering or filtering by timestamp window inside get_request_data will silently alter later pages' error output; the sort should happen once at construction.

adjudication.rationale: In `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `get_request_data(iterator, error_events)` does `error_events.sort(...)` in place. That same `error_events` list is created once in the endpoint `get()` and then captured in `functools.partial(analyze_recording_segments, error_events)` passed as `paginate(..., on_results=...)`, meaning the same mutable list instance is reused across per-page `on_results` invocations. Today the in-place sort is effectively idempotent and doesn’t break current behavior, but the diff does introduce shared mutable state across pages, and any future per-page mutation/filtering based on timestamps would be order/contents-dependent and could affect later pages. Sorting once before constructing the partial (or sorting a copy inside `get_request_data`) would avoid this latent footgun.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new enable_error_context=false gating uses default-true truthy string comparison, but the diff does not document or test the sibling behavior that error context fetch runs an unconditional nodestore.get_multi plus a Snuba query_replay_instance call on every request even when no errors exist. Every summarize request now pays a full replay-instance Snuba query plus a nodestore multi-get regardless of whether any error IDs exist; clients on the old path (no error context support) get a hot-path latency regression with no way to disable the Snuba query itself — only the nodestore fetch is gated by the query param.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the code unconditionally calls `query_replay_instance(...)` and `process_raw_response(...)` to extract `error_ids` before checking `enable_error_context` (see added block starting with `snuba_response = query_replay_instance(...)`). The `enable_error_context=false` param only gates the subsequent `fetch_error_details(...)` nodestore lookup, not the Snuba replay-instance query itself. Also, when enabled, `fetch_error_details` will still call `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` even if `error_ids` is an empty list (no guard beyond the try/except). The added tests cover disabling error context affecting the logs sent to Seer, but do not assert/cover the “no errors” path or the unconditional Snuba query behavior. This is a concrete performance/latency concern introduced by the diff, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] This PR, titled 'Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System', flips the global default of DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT from "low" to "off" (and the corresponding projectoption in src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py line 205), which is unrelated to replay deletion and is a user-visible behavior change for every org not pinning the option. Orgs relying on the default get autofix silently disabled after this deploy; whoever merges this for the replay-delete feature ships an unrequested behavioral change to all customers and cannot trace it to any stated requirement.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes the default autofix automation tuning from "low" to "off" in both backend constants (`src/sentry/constants.py`: `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT`) and the persisted project option default (`src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py`: `register(key="sentry:autofix_automation_tuning", default="off")`). That is a user-visible, global behavior change for any project/org relying on defaults, and it is not obviously related to the other changes in this PR (which include many replay/devservices/explore/etc changes). This is a legitimate scope/release-risk concern rather than a code correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Two shipped data migrations (0917 and 0920 converting org saved searches to views) are gutted to `return`, dead-code removal that has nothing to do with the stated replay bulk-delete intent. Ops engineers reviewing this PR for replay deletion will miss that a data migration was retroactively disabled; the change belongs in its own PR with its own justification, and bundling it hides a data-integrity decision from reviewers of the replay feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows both `src/sentry/migrations/0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py` and `0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py` were changed from performing DB data conversion into immediate no-ops (`return`) with comments claiming they were erroneous/never run and pointing to `0921_...` as the correct migration. Regardless of correctness, this is a significant, nontrivial change in migration behavior (retroactively disabling shipped migrations) that is orthogonal to the replay bulk-delete changes also present in the PR, and could be missed by reviewers focused elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The removal of ParameterizationRegexExperiment, the corresponding option registration in src/sentry/options/defaults.py (lines 2627-2632), and the isinstance dispatch simplification is a grouping-engine refactor unrelated to the replay bulk-delete intent of this PR. Anyone bisecting a grouping regression or auditing feature-flag cleanup now lands on a 'replays bulk delete' commit; the coupling also means reverting the replay feature reverts the grouping experiment teardown.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly includes a grouping-engine refactor: `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` is removed from `src/sentry/grouping/parameterization.py`, the `ParameterizationExperiment` union is narrowed, the `isinstance` dispatch is simplified, related option registration `grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent` is deleted from `src/sentry/options/defaults.py`, and associated tests are removed in `tests/sentry/grouping/test_parameterization.py`. The diff also includes replay bulk-delete-related changes (e.g., `src/sentry/replays/usecases/delete.py` handling `max_segment_id: None`). Bundling these unrelated changes into the same PR/commit is a valid scope/maintainability concern (it affects bisection/reverts), but it is not, by itself, a verifiable functional defect introduced by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The endpoint is rewritten from a dataclass to a DRF serializer with new validation semantics (age/timestamp mutual exclusion, per-report 422 responses), which is unrelated to replay bulk delete. The PR's stated scope gives reviewers of browser reporting no context — the new mutual-exclusion validation rejects reports browsers legitimately send (e.g., an Editor's Draft report carrying both fields is silently dropped as 422), a contract change smuggled in under an unrelated title.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly rewrites `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint` from constructing a `BrowserReport` dataclass to validating each entry with a new `BrowserReportSerializer` and adds new semantics: it now hard-rejects payloads that include both `age` and `timestamp` via `validate_timestamp` / `validate_age`, returning a 422 with error details (`HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY`). This is a behavior/contract change (tests assert it in `test_mixed_fields`) and is mixed into a PR that also changes replay deletion logic, so it’s valid to flag as scope creep / needing clearer context. However, the finding’s claim that such reports are “silently dropped” is incorrect (the code returns an explicit 422 response with details). Whether browsers “legitimately” send both fields cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] This diff substantially extends the breadcrumb summarization endpoint with error-event fetching, chronological merging, and a new `enable_error_context` query param — feature work adjacent to but distinct from the stated bulk-delete system. The new undocumented raw query param `enable_error_context` (line ~83) is behavior with no requirement traceability and no feature flag; it rides along in a PR whose title promises only deletion, so its Snuba/nodestore call additions on every GET are unreviewed as a scope item.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does materially expand `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get` to (a) query replay instance data via `query_replay_instance(...)` and `process_raw_response(...)` to derive `error_ids`, and (b) fetch full error event payloads from nodestore (`nodestore.backend.get_multi(...)`) and merge them chronologically into the prompt (`gen_request_data(...)`). It also introduces a new query param `enable_error_context` (defaulting to "true") to skip error fetching, but this param is not tied to a dedicated feature flag (the endpoint is still gated by existing replay/AI feature checks). Additionally, the Snuba replay-instance query is executed unconditionally before checking `enable_error_context`, so there is extra per-GET work even when error context is disabled. These are legitimate scope/architecture/review-surface concerns grounded in the diff, though they are not a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Adding processing_deadline_duration (30/300/120) to webhook delivery taskworker configs, plus the similar deadline added in src/sentry/tasks/auth/check_auth.py, is infrastructure tuning unrelated to the replay bulk-delete system. These deadline changes alter task retry/redelivery semantics for webhooks and auth checks; bundled into a replay PR they bypass the scrutiny of the owners of those subsystems, and a revert of the replay feature silently reverts them.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `processing_deadline_duration` to multiple taskworker configs in subsystems unrelated to replay bulk delete: `src/sentry/hybridcloud/tasks/deliver_webhooks.py` (30/300/120 seconds for `schedule_webhook_delivery`, `drain_mailbox`, `drain_mailbox_parallel`) and `src/sentry/tasks/auth/check_auth.py` (60 seconds for `check_auth_identities`). The finding’s concern is about cross-cutting infrastructure/operational tuning being bundled with other changes (including replay-related work elsewhere in the diff), which is a scope/ownership/review-scrutiny issue rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The GitHub/GitLab merged-PR comment template is redesigned (new template constant, title truncation, environment suffix) — user-facing integration output changes with no traceability to the replay bulk-delete requirement. Every customer with the GitHub/GitLab PR bot gets differently formatted PR comments after this deploy; the change also adds a per-issue `get_recommended_event()` call on the comment path (line 585), a new DB/nodestore cost on a hot integration path hidden inside an unrelated PR.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes the GitHub/GitLab merged-PR comment formatting by moving the template to `integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py` (`MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE`), adding title truncation, and appending an environment suffix (GitHub/GitLab now call `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(..., environment=self.get_environment_info(issue))`). `get_environment_info` newly calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` per issue, which can plausibly add extra lookup cost on the PR comment path. This is a concrete scope/perf/behavior change visible in the diff, but not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The workflow-engine refactor (hoisting get_slow_conditions_for_groups, threading dcg_to_slow_conditions through two functions, swapping logger to log_context in processors/workflow.py) is untraceable to any replay bulk-delete requirement. Workflow engine owners get semantics changes (including a new info-level log on no-slow-condition DCGs) shipped under a replay PR title; this makes blame/bisect and selective revert of the actual feature impossible.

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes workflow-engine changes unrelated to replay bulk-delete: in `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/delayed_workflow.py` the slow-condition lookup is hoisted into `process_delayed_workflows`, threaded through `get_condition_query_groups(..., dcg_to_slow_conditions)` and `get_groups_to_fire(..., dcg_to_slow_conditions)`, and a new info-level log `delayed_workflow.no_slow_condition_groups` is added. Separately, `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/workflow.py` changes the logger to `log_context.get_logger(__name__)`. These are real scope/traceability concerns (semantics/logging changes shipped alongside replay work) but not a verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New analytics event registration and instrumentation of the preprod artifact assemble endpoint is unrelated scope riding in this PR. Analytics event schema decisions land unreviewed by the preprod/telemetry owners; a revert of the replay feature would silently remove the event, breaking dashboards built on it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new analytics event and instrumentation for the preprod artifact assemble endpoint: `src/sentry/preprod/analytics.py` registers `PreprodArtifactApiAssembleEvent` and `src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py` calls `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)`. This change is orthogonal to many other areas touched in the PR (replays, explore, workflow engine, etc.), so the “scope riding”/ownership-review concern is diff-grounded. The warning about future reverts potentially removing this newly-added event is also plausible given it’s added in this PR, though the mention of a specific “replay feature” revert is not directly evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Rewriting the feedback-summary LLM prompt (separator change, 55-word hard cap) is unrelated to the stated replay bulk-delete intent. Prompt engineering changes materially alter AI output for all feedback-summary users and cannot be tested by this PR's replay-delete review; bundling them makes the change effectively unreviewed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes material prompt-engineering changes in `src/sentry/feedback/usecases/feedback_summaries.py` (changing the feedback separator from bullet list to `\n------\n`, adding a strict "AT MOST 55 words" / "AT MOST two sentences" requirement, and altering instructions to avoid generic statements). These changes will affect feedback-summary AI output and are unrelated to the replay bulk-delete-related changes elsewhere (e.g., `src/sentry/replays/usecases/delete.py` handling `max_segment_id is None`). While the PR's "stated intent" isn't visible in the diff, the finding’s core point—unrelated, behavior-changing LLM prompt edits bundled into a large PR—is diff-grounded and a legitimate scope/reviewability concern rather than a direct correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Adding an `equations` passthrough parameter to run_top_events_timeseries_query is API-surface work for the logs dataset with no requirement traceability in a replay bulk-delete PR. The new parameter is accepted but no call site in this diff passes it — a ships-inert signature change that logs-dataset owners never reviewed under this PR's scope.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new optional `equations: list[str] | None = None` parameter to `src/sentry/snuba/ourlogs.py::run_top_events_timeseries_query` and forwards it into `rpc_dataset_common.run_top_events_timeseries_query(..., equations=equations)`. Within the provided diff, there is no new/updated call site passing `equations`, so this is effectively an API/signature surface expansion without demonstrated usage or accompanying tests in this PR. While not a verifiable functional defect (it’s backward-compatible and defaults to None), it is a scope/ownership/traceability concern grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details zips error_ids against events.values() of the nodestore.get_multi result, so when any node_id is missing from the returned dict, the remaining ids get paired with the wrong events' data. For a replay with one or more error events purged from nodestore, every subsequent id/data pair is shifted by one, so the LLM breadcrumb summary attributes the wrong title/message to the wrong error and can misorder errors entirely; a simple `[(id, events.get(node_id)) for id in error_ids]` lookup keyed by node_id would be correct.

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details` (new code in `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`), it builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, then pairs IDs to data via `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. Since `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node_id and may omit missing entries, `events.values()` can be shorter and no longer positionally aligned with `error_ids`, causing subsequent IDs to be matched to the wrong event data (or dropped due to zip truncation). The finding’s suggested fix (lookup by node_id per error_id) is consistent with the diff and would avoid misattribution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] gen_request_data interleaves error timestamps against rrweb segment event timestamps that are on different scales/types: nodestore event `timestamp` is a second-scale value (often an ISO string, per data.get('timestamp')), while segment events carry millisecond-epoch numbers, so the comparison `error_events[error_idx]['timestamp'] < event.get('timestamp', 0)` compares incomparable units (and can raise TypeError comparing str to int). Error log messages are emitted at the wrong positions in the interleaved chronology (or the endpoint 500s when a string timestamp is compared against an int), so the breadcrumb summary sent to Seer reports errors out of order relative to user actions; the fetch must normalize both to one unit before sorting/interleaving.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new logic in `gen_request_data` that interleaves replay segment events with nodestore-derived error events by sorting and comparing `error_events[*]["timestamp"]` against `event.get("timestamp", 0)` with no normalization or type coercion (see `error_events.sort(...)` and `while ... < event.get(...)`). `fetch_error_details` pulls `timestamp` straight from nodestore (`data.get("timestamp", 0.0)`), so if that value is not a numeric in the same unit as rrweb event timestamps, ordering will be wrong or comparisons could fail. The diff itself doesn’t prove rrweb timestamps are ms or nodestore timestamps are strings, so the specific unit-mismatch claim can’t be fully verified, but the lack of normalization between two timestamp sources is a real, diff-grounded risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new DRF serializer makes `body` a required DictField and `url` a required URLField, which is a narrowing of the previously-accepted report shape: the Reporting API spec permits reports whose `body` is absent (e.g. crash and some policy reports) and an empty `url`, all of which the old dataclass constructor accepted. Browsers sending spec-legal reports with no body or empty url now receive HTTP 422 instead of 200, so those reports are silently dropped and the collector's metric undercounts real browser reports; body should be required=False/allow_null and url should tolerate empty string per the spec.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the endpoint now validates reports with a DRF `BrowserReportSerializer` where `url = serializers.URLField()` and `body = serializers.DictField()` are required and `url` must be a valid URL, returning 422 on validation failure. Previously it did `BrowserReport(**report)` with no URL validation, so empty/invalid `url` strings (if present) would have been accepted and counted. However, the finding’s claim that the old code accepted reports with `body` absent is not supported: the old `BrowserReport` dataclass required `body` and would have raised on missing fields. Whether the stricter validation violates the Reporting API spec cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators use truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")`), so `age: 0` is treated as absent and a report carrying both `timestamp` and `age: 0` passes validation, and a report with neither field is also accepted even though the spec requires exactly one. Malformed reports that violate the Working-Draft/Editor's-Draft split leak into the metrics tag path and skew counts; the next editor debugging 'which spec sent this report' gets misleading data.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer` (src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py), the mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness: `if self.initial_data.get("age")` in `validate_timestamp` and `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")` in `validate_age`. This means `age: 0` (or `timestamp: 0`) is treated as “absent”, so a payload with both `timestamp` and `age: 0` can pass validation. Also, since both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False` and there is no object-level validation enforcing exactly one, a report with neither field is accepted. This is a correctness issue in the new validation logic introduced by the diff; existing tests only cover non-zero mixed fields.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The preprod_artifact.api.assemble analytics event is recorded before the feature-gate check, so unauthorized and feature-disabled requests are counted identically to real assembles. Whoever consumes this analytics event to measure assemble adoption gets inflated counts including 403-gated requests; move the record() after the features.has check.
matched_golden_ids: Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying problem: the analytics event is recorded before the feature flag/gate check, so requests that should be blocked (feature-disabled/unauthorized, including those returning 404/403) still emit the event, inflating/misleading analytics. Candidate even suggests moving record() after the features.has check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `enable_error_context` flag is parsed as a raw query string compared with `.lower() == "false"` (default "true"), a stringly-typed boolean with no named constant and no shared client/server definition, so any other falsy value ("0", "False" handled, but "no", "off", empty string) silently means true. The next caller toggling the flag with a value other than the exact string 'false' gets error context silently included and has no compile-checked constant to discover the contract from.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, the new logic uses `request.query_params.get("enable_error_context", "true").lower() == "false"` to disable error fetching. This establishes a string contract where only the literal (case-insensitive) value "false" disables error context; other common boolean-ish values (e.g., "0", "off", empty string) will not disable it and will silently include error context. The finding accurately describes this stringly-typed API contract risk introduced by the diff, but it’s more of an API/UX robustness concern than a verifiable functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with nodestore results via zip(error_ids, events.values()), but get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id that drops missing nodes, so positional pairing misassigns titles/messages/timestamps to the wrong error_id. When any requested event is absent from nodestore, every subsequent error event in the list is labeled with the wrong event id and wrong title, so the LLM breadcrumb summary attributes one error's message to another error.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids` and calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, which returns a dict keyed by node id. The code then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`, pairing IDs with dict values purely by iteration order and length, rather than by key. If `get_multi` omits missing keys and/or does not guarantee value ordering to match the input list, the `event_id` can be paired with the wrong event payload, causing misattributed titles/messages/timestamps in the generated error log messages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, and PRCommentWorkflow is a separate ABC that does not inherit from it, so the call raises AttributeError. Every merged-PR comment containing at least one issue (GitHub and GitLab) crashes with AttributeError instead of rendering the comment body.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py`, the new `CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template()` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, but `_truncate_title` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration` (as a `@staticmethod`) in this same diff. Unless `PRCommentWorkflow` separately defines `_truncate_title` (not shown in the diff), this will raise `AttributeError` when generating merged-PR issue list items, breaking GitHub/GitLab PR comment rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The default for sentry:autofix_automation_tuning is silently flipped from "low" to "off" (also in src/sentry/constants.py:724) inside a PR titled "Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System", with no feature flag or migration for projects that relied on the old default. All existing projects that never explicitly set the option stop getting autofix automation on new issues after deploy; this product-behavior change has no explicit acceptance trail in the PR's stated objective and cannot be rolled back without a code deploy.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does verifiably change the default autofix automation tuning from "low" to "off" in both `src/sentry/constants.py` (DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT) and `src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py` (register default), and updates tests to expect "off". The finding’s concern that this flips behavior for projects that never explicitly set the option is plausible given the default change, but the diff alone can’t prove whether a feature flag/migration/rollout exists elsewhere or whether the change is intentional. This is a real, diff-grounded review concern about product behavior/rollout rather than a strictly provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 0917 and 0920 data migrations' conversion logic is deleted and replaced with a no-op `return` while the migration numbers are retained, relying on a comment asserting they were never run; any environment that did execute the buggy version will have its partially-converted state silently frozen. Deployments where the original migration ran with data errors keep corrupted/partial GroupSearchView rows with no idempotent re-run, and org-level saved searches remain unconverted; the fix depends entirely on the unverifiable claim that 0921 covers every environment.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes both data migrations `0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py` and `0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py` to no-op functions that immediately `return`, while keeping the same migration numbers and adding comments asserting they were never run. That is a real, diff-grounded risk/operational concern: if any deployment actually applied these migrations previously (or applied them partially), this change provides no remediation path within those migration numbers and relies on an external later migration (mentioned as 0921, not shown here). However, the finding’s claims about environments having executed the buggy migrations and being left in a corrupted/partial state cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Neither age nor timestamp is required by the serializer, so a report containing neither field validates successfully, contradicting the Working-Draft-vs-Editor's-Draft mutual-exclusion intent the cross-validation was written to enforce. Malformed browser reports missing both fields are accepted with HTTP 200 and counted in metrics, so the collector's validation figures overstate real report volume and downstream consumers assuming a timestamp get None.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer` (browser_reporting_collector.py), both `age` and `timestamp` are declared `required=False`, and the only cross-validation is mutual exclusion via `validate_timestamp`/`validate_age`. If a report includes neither field, neither validator runs and the serializer will accept the report as valid. The endpoint then increments `browser_reporting.raw_report_received` and returns 200 for that report. This matches the finding’s core claim that malformed reports missing both fields are accepted, undermining the intended spec-variant validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The merged-PR comment format silently changed from `- ‼️ **{title}** \`{subtitle}\` [View Issue]({url})` to `* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}`, dropping the culprit subtitle entirely, with no visible acceptance that removing culprit context from PR comments is intended. Users who relied on the culprit line in merged-PR comments lose that signal after deploy with no feature gate or release note in this PR's stated objective.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the old `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE` that included the culprit subtitle (GitHub/GitLab integrations) and replaces formatting with `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE = "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n"` in `commit_context.py`, with callers now passing `environment=self.get_environment_info(issue)` and no longer passing/formatting `issue.culprit` at all. Tests were updated to match the new output. This is a deliberate behavior/output change rather than an inherent correctness bug, but the concern about un-gated UX/product impact is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new validation-failure path logs the entire raw attacker-supplied report body (`extra={..."raw_report": report}`) at warning level. Browser reports contain page URLs, user agents, and CSP violation details (which can include injected query-string values from end users); anyone on the internet can POST arbitrary payloads to this CSRF-exempt, unauthenticated endpoint, filling logs with attacker-chosen content and potential PII at unbounded volume — log injection/PII-leak vector introduced by this diff's logging call.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py`, the new validation failure branch logs attacker-controlled input at warning level: `logger.warning(..., extra={"validation_errors": serializer.errors, "raw_report": report})`. This endpoint is explicitly `@csrf_exempt` with `permission_classes = ()`, so any unauthenticated internet client can POST arbitrary payloads. The logged `report` can include URLs, user agents, and arbitrary JSON values, creating a concrete PII leakage / log-injection / log-volume amplification vector introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template interpolates raw, unescaped issue titles and environment names into a Markdown template that is posted to GitHub/GitLab PR comments. Issue titles and environment names originate from ingested events (attacker-controllable by anyone who can send events to the project); a title containing Markdown/HTML link syntax (e.g. `[click](https://evil.example)` or an image tag) is rendered as-is in the bot's PR comment on the customer's repository, enabling content spoofing/link injection through a trusted Sentry bot account.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py`, `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE = "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n"` and `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template()` formats `title` (from `issue.title`) and `environment` (from `recommended_event.get_environment().name` via `get_environment_info()`) directly into Markdown without escaping. Since `title` and `environment` are not sanitized (only truncated), a crafted title/environment containing Markdown control characters (e.g. `](`, backticks) could alter the rendered PR comment posted by the bot, enabling link/content injection in GitHub/GitLab comments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with nodestore results by position instead of key: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` zips the request order against a dict's values, and nodestore.backend.get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id that omits (or None-fills) missing nodes, so once any node is missing or the dict ordering differs from error_ids, the wrong event's title/message is attached to the wrong error id. The `if data is not None` guard filters the shifted pairs, so the endpoint silently reports the wrong error title/message for a given error id (or drops valid errors) whenever one of the fetched nodes is missing — exactly the case the None guard exists for.

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details` (new in `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`), the code does `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then builds results via `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. Since `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by `node_id` and may omit missing nodes, `events.values()` can be shorter and/or not aligned with `error_ids` by position. If any node is missing (the exact case handled by `if data is not None`), `zip` shifts subsequent pairings and attaches the wrong title/message/timestamp to the wrong `error_id`, or drops valid errors. Correct pairing should be by key (e.g., lookup by the corresponding node_id per error_id).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators use truthiness (`if self.initial_data.get("age")`) and neither field is required, so a report with age=0 and a timestamp, or a report with neither age nor timestamp, passes validation despite violating the 'exactly one of the two' spec semantics the comments claim to enforce. Clients sending age=0 alongside a timestamp (legitimate per the Working Draft) get an incorrect 422, and malformed reports with neither field are accepted with HTTP 200 and counted in metrics, skewing the browser_report_type adoption figures this endpoint was instrumented to gather.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer` (src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py), the mutual-exclusion logic uses truthiness checks: `validate_timestamp` does `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` does `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. This fails to detect presence when the other field is `0` (e.g., `age=0` or `timestamp=0`), allowing both fields to be provided without triggering validation errors. Also, since both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False` and there is no serializer-level `validate()` enforcing "exactly one", a report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` will still pass `is_valid()` and be counted in metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new null check for max_segment_id returns an empty filename list, silently skipping deletion of recording segment files whenever the ClickHouse aggregate returns NULL, which conflates 'no segments tracked in the aggregate' with 'no segment files exist in blob storage'. Replays that have recording segment files in object storage but a NULL max_segment_id (due to delayed aggregate computation, backfill gaps, or replays whose rows pre-date segment tracking) will have their segment files permanently retained past the retention window or after a GDPR deletion request — silent data retention violation with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/usecases/delete.py`, `_make_recording_filenames` now does `if row["max_segment_id"] is None: return []`, which changes behavior from throwing (e.g., `range(None + 1)` TypeError) to silently skipping segment-file deletion for that replay row. The diff itself supports the “silent skip” aspect (no logging/metrics/error) and the conflation risk is plausible because `max_segment_id` is now explicitly `int | None` and the code assumes `None` == “no segments ingested.” However, the diff does not prove that `NULL` can occur while segment files still exist in storage, so the strong claim about guaranteed retention/GDPR violation cannot be fully verified from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Two shipped migration files (0917 and 0920) are gutted into no-ops and defer all conversion to 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py, which is not visible in the shown diff — if any self-hosted deployment already applied the original 0917 or 0920 migrations, the django_migrations table marks them as applied while the file content no longer performs the work, and correctness depends entirely on 0921 being present and idempotent. Self-hosted operators upgrading through this change must trust that 0921 exists, covers the same data set with the corrected filter, and uses an idempotent upsert; if 0921 is missing, mis-ordered in the migration graph, or has a narrower WHERE clause than the originals, org-level saved searches are silently lost during upgrade with no error and no rollback path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes two existing migration files (`0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py` and `0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py`) from performing data migration work to immediate no-ops (`return`), and even deletes the test that asserted 0917’s behavior. Both files now rely on a separate migration (`0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`) that is referenced in comments but is not present in the shown diff, so a reviewer can’t verify ordering/idempotence/coverage from what’s provided. However, the finding’s claim about already-applied migrations becoming “correctness depends entirely on 0921” is partly speculative given the diff alone (we can’t see 0921), so this is best treated as an important migration-safety concern rather than a provable defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Gutting 0920 (which added the owner_id__isnull=False filter over 0917) creates a migration-history hazard: any environment that partially applied 0917 before erroring will have some SavedSearch rows already converted to GroupSearchView, and the surviving update_or_create in 0921 must use the exact same natural-key lookup (organization, user_id, name) to avoid creating duplicate GroupSearchView rows for the same SavedSearch. If 0921's lookup key or filter differs from the originals, partial converts from a failed 0917 run produce duplicate or orphaned GroupSearchView entries that surface to end users as duplicated saved searches in the Issues UI after upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show 0917 and 0920 being replaced with no-op functions (with comments claiming they were never run) and the deletion of the 0917 migration test, but the finding’s core claim depends on the contents/behavior of `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py` (e.g., whether its `update_or_create` lookup/filter matches 0917/0920). That 0921 migration is not included in the diff, so we cannot verify the asserted duplication/orphan hazard or any mismatch in natural-key lookup from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] validate_timestamp/validate_age use truthiness checks on `self.initial_data.get("age")` / `.get("timestamp")` so a legitimate value of 0 is treated as absent, defeating the mutual-exclusion validation entirely. A report sending `age: 0` alongside `timestamp` passes validate_timestamp's guard (0 is falsy) and is accepted with both fields present, so the spec-invariant the code claims to enforce is silently violated; symmetrically `timestamp: 0` is treated as absent and a report carrying both age and timestamp=0 is accepted instead of 422.
matched_golden_ids: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same underlying bug: using truthiness checks via `self.initial_data.get('age')`/`get('timestamp')` causes legitimate `0` values to be treated as missing, which breaks the mutual-exclusion validation (including the `timestamp=0` case highlighted in the golden comment).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The validation error message in validate_timestamp is inverted relative to the check: it raises when a timestamp is present and age is ALSO present, but the text says "If timestamp is present, age must be absent" — and validate_age's message describes the opposite field pair, so the 422 body misdescribes which field is at fault. A client sending both fields gets a message blaming timestamp validation when the conflicting field is age (and vice versa from validate_age), misdirecting integrators debugging rejected reports; the error shape is right but the content names the wrong field.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer`, `validate_timestamp` only runs when `timestamp` is present, and it raises iff `age` is also present: `if self.initial_data.get("age"):` then error "If timestamp is present, age must be absent"—which correctly describes the conflict. Symmetrically, `validate_age` runs when `age` is present and errors if `timestamp` is also present with the correct message. The accompanying test `test_mixed_fields` expects both field errors with these exact messages, matching the implementation, so there is no inverted/misdirected validation message in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details zips `error_ids` against `events.values()` from nodestore.get_multi, but get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id containing only the found nodes, so when any node is missing the remaining values shift position and are paired with the wrong error IDs. When one or more error events are missing/evicted from nodestore, every subsequent error ID in the list is paired with a different event's data (wrong title, message, timestamp), and the resulting summary request silently mixes up which errors occurred — corrupt AI-generated context with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details` (new in `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`), the code does `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then pairs results via `zip(error_ids, events.values())`, ignoring the returned dict's keys. This implicitly relies on `get_multi` returning a dict whose values are in the same order as the input `node_ids` and (crucially) that missing node_ids are still represented (e.g., mapped to `None`) rather than omitted. The diff does not show `get_multi`’s contract/implementation, so the finding’s specific claim (“only the found nodes, causing shifting”) can’t be definitively verified from the PR alone, but the ordering/omission assumption is a concrete, diff-grounded correctness risk worth addressing by looking up by `node_id` instead of zipping against `.values()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] fetch_error_details catches Exception broadly, reports via sentry_sdk.capture_exception, and returns [] so the summarize endpoint proceeds with breadcrumbs only, silently dropping all error context. Users of the replay summarization feature get a breadcrumb-only summary with no indication that error context was requested and failed, and operators only see it if they sample the capture_exception; a persistent nodestore outage degrades every summary silently.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `fetch_error_details()` wraps the entire nodestore fetch in `try: ... except Exception as e:` and on any error calls `sentry_sdk.capture_exception(e)` then returns `[]`. The calling endpoint (`get()`) then proceeds to `analyze_recording_segments` with `error_events=[]`, producing a breadcrumbs-only request to Seer without indicating that error context retrieval failed (unless the query param disables it). This is a real, diff-grounded resilience/observability concern (silent degradation) but not a directly verifiable correctness defect given the code intentionally falls back.
